comparison: Perfect agreement on colocalization of chemotaxis complex and flagella (C4, C35, C36, C89, C90). Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and well-supported by fluorescence imaging data showing consistent colocalization in all observed cells.

Strong agreement on FlhF's role in polar localization (C5, C41-C48, C93, C97, C98). Both accept that FlhF affects polar distribution but not colocalization itself. OpenEval includes C109 which peer review groups elsewhere. Both find the quantitative data and Western blot controls convincing.

Agreement on motor structure requirement for chemoreceptor assembly (C6, C54-C57, C100, C104, C108, C110). Both accept the distinction between structural integrity and motor function. OpenEval notes mechanism remains unclear, while peer review accepts conclusions without this caveat. OpenEval includes additional claims (C58, C60, C68, C69) that peer review groups with other results.

Complete agreement on CheY overexpression causing c-di-GMP elevation and aggregation (C7, C8, C73-C75, C84, C87). Both evaluations find the biosensor data, dose-dependent effects, and PDE rescue experiments convincing and well-supported.

Divergent evaluations of functional significance claims (C9, C115-C119, C121, C122). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic link is inferential and lacks direct experimental validation. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, finding the signaling crosstalk argument plausible. This represents the most significant disagreement between evaluations.

Agreement on bipolar assembly observations in pre-division cells (C37, C38, C91, C92). Both accept the observational data. OpenEval notes functional consequences are inferred rather than directly tested, while peer review accepts conclusions without this qualification.

Partial overlap on reciprocal experiments (C61, C107). OpenEval groups these as establishing independence and specificity. Peer review includes these claims within a broader set of supporting quantitative measurements (R6) that also encompasses Western blots and other controls.

Partial overlap on membrane curvature interpretation (C70, C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the interpretation is speculative with alternative explanations not excluded. Peer review includes these claims in a broader SUPPORTED evaluation of supporting measurements without expressing concern about the interpretation.

Partial overlap on CheY-eYFP localization (C32, C33). OpenEval groups these with validation data (C131, C132) as a methodological validation result. Peer review includes C32, C33 within broader supporting quantitative measurements. Both find the data convincing.

Partial overlap on methodology (C125, C126). OpenEval focuses on experimental approach documentation. Peer review's R7 includes these claims plus validation data (C131, C132) in a broader methodological acceptance. Both find methods appropriate and well-documented.

Partial overlap on CheY-eYFP validation (C131, C132). OpenEval groups with localization data (C32, C33) to validate the marker. Peer review includes these in broader methodological acceptance (R7) with C125, C126. Both accept the validation without challenge.

OpenEval evaluates timescale comparison claims (C77-C81) arguing against enhanced chemotaxis as primary function. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these claims were not explicitly addressed in peer reviews.
